name: Ryobi ONE+ 18V WhisperSeries 7-1/2 in. Fan (PCL811B)
amazonQuery: Ryobi PCL811B ONE+ 18V WhisperSeries 7-1/2 in. fan
summary: A quiet 7-1/2 inch hybrid fan that runs on any Ryobi ONE+ 18V battery or a plain extension cord; the best outage fan for anyone who already owns ONE+ packs.
verdict:
The Ryobi PCL811B is the battery fan most households should buy first, because it runs on the ONE+ 18V packs that millions of people already own and it is quiet enough to sleep beside.

**It is a hybrid, so it works every day.** The fan runs on any ONE+ 18V battery, or it plugs into an ordinary extension cord while the grid is up. That means it earns shelf space all summer, not just during an outage. Ryobi sells it bare (PCL811B) or in kits with a 2Ah (PCL811K) or 4Ah (PCL811K1) battery and charger.

**Quiet is the point.** Ryobi says the WhisperSeries version is 44% quieter with 24% more air velocity than the fan it replaced. It has three speeds, listed at 930, 1,500 and 1,850 RPM, and a 160° pivoting head with a handle and hanging options. The 7-1/2 inch blade is personal-scale: one sleeper, a desk or a tent corner, not a whole living room.

**Do the battery math.** A 4Ah ONE+ pack holds about 72 [watt-hours](/glossary/watt-hours/). Ryobi does not publish a runtime, but if the fan draws around 10 watts on a middle speed, one pack lasts roughly seven hours, and low stretches that further. Charge spare packs from a [power station](/gear/jackery-explorer-1000-v2/); the [runtime calculator](/tools/power-station-runtime-calculator/) shows how many refills you get.

Owners report it is genuinely quiet on low and easy to hang from a bunk or tent loop. The main complaint is modest airflow on high next to jobsite fans like the [DeWalt DCE512B](/gear/dewalt-20v-max-jobsite-fan/). It is the top pick in our [best battery-powered fan](/best-battery-powered-fan/) roundup.
bestFor: Quiet bedside cooling for anyone who already owns Ryobi ONE+ batteries

faqs.q: How long does the Ryobi WhisperSeries fan run on a battery?
faqs.a: It depends on the pack and the speed. Ryobi does not publish one runtime figure, but the math is simple: a 4Ah ONE+ battery stores about 72 watt-hours, so if the fan draws around 10 watts on a middle setting, one pack lasts roughly seven hours. Low speed stretches that, and a 6Ah pack adds about half again.

faqs.q: What is the difference between the Ryobi PCL811 and the Ryobi bucket top misting fan?
faqs.a: The PCL811 is a standalone 7-1/2 inch fan with a 160° pivoting head that runs on a ONE+ battery or an extension cord. The PCL851 bucket top fan sits on a 5-gallon bucket and adds a water mist, rated for up to 14 feet of misting coverage. Pick the PCL811 for indoor sleeping and the misting fan for patios and yard work.

name: DeWalt DCE512B 20V MAX Jobsite Fan
summary: DeWalt's 11-inch cordless jobsite fan, rated at up to 650 CFM and IP54, is the pick for garages, attics and whole-room airflow if you already run 20V MAX batteries.
verdict:
The DeWalt DCE512B is the strongest everyday battery fan here for anyone on the 20V MAX platform: it moves room-scale air and shrugs off jobsite abuse.

**Real airflow from a battery.** DeWalt rates the 11-inch fan at up to 650 CFM with variable speed control, about 30% more than the DCE511B it replaced. That is enough to clear paint fumes from a garage, dry a damp room or keep a family room tolerable when the AC is down. It carries an IP54 rating against dust and water spray, and it can stand freely, hang from its hook or mount on a wall.

**Runtime means bigger packs.** DeWalt lists up to 4.5 hours at maximum airspeed with a 5Ah battery. A 5Ah 20V MAX pack holds about 90 [watt-hours](/glossary/watt-hours/) at its 18V nominal rating, so plan on one pack per evening on high and far longer at lower speeds. Two packs and a charger fed by a [power station](/gear/anker-solix-c1000/) or a [generator](/best-gas-generator/) keep it running through a multi-day outage.

**Cordless only, and louder.** Unlike the older DCE511, the DCE512B has no AC input, so it always needs a battery. It weighs about 6 pounds and stands 16 inches tall. It is louder than bedside fans such as the [Ryobi WhisperSeries](/gear/ryobi-one-plus-whisperseries-fan/), so it suits a living area better than a pillow.

Owners report strong airflow and a tough housing; the most common complaints are noise on high and no published low-speed runtime. See where it ranks in the [best battery-powered fan](/best-battery-powered-fan/) roundup.

name: Milwaukee M12 Mounting Fan (0820-20)
summary: Milwaukee's 6-inch M12 fan clamps, hangs or sticks magnetically almost anywhere and runs up to 16 hours on an XC 6.0 pack; a smart outage fan for M12 owners.
verdict:
The Milwaukee 0820-20 is the right fan for anyone already carrying M12 batteries, and its mounting options make it more useful than its size suggests.

**Mount it anywhere.** Milwaukee builds in strong magnets, a 2-inch spring-loaded clamp, keyholes and pass-through holes, and the head rotates 360°. In an outage you can clip it to a headboard, stick it to a steel door frame or hang it from a closet rod, aimed right at the person who needs it. Older listings call it the M12 Jobsite Fan; it is the same 0820-20.

**Small battery, long runtime.** Milwaukee rates it at 400 CFM and up to 14 MPH from a 6-inch blade, with three speeds. Runtime is the standout: up to 16 hours on an M12 XC 6.0 battery. That pack holds about 72 [watt-hours](/glossary/watt-hours/) at 12V, the same as a 4Ah 18V pack, so a full night on one battery is realistic. A 2Ah compact pack holds about 24 Wh, so expect about a third of the runtime.

**Know its limits.** It is a personal and spot fan, not a room fan. For more air on the same brand, look at the [Milwaukee M18 PACKOUT Fan](/gear/milwaukee-m18-packout-fan/). If you own no Milwaukee packs, the [Ryobi WhisperSeries](/gear/ryobi-one-plus-whisperseries-fan/) or a built-in-battery fan is a cheaper start.

Owners report the magnets and clamp are the reason to buy it; the main complaint is that it is tool-only, so batteries add up. It appears in our [best battery-powered fan](/best-battery-powered-fan/) roundup.

faqs.q: What is the difference between the Milwaukee M12 fan and the M18 PACKOUT fan?
faqs.a: Size and airflow. The M12 0820-20 is a 6-inch, 400 CFM mounting fan with magnets and a clamp, rated for up to 16 hours on an XC 6.0 pack. The M18 PACKOUT fan 0818-20 is rated at 850 CFM and can run on AC power, but Milwaukee quotes just over 3 hours on high with an XC5.0 pack.

name: O2COOL Treva 10-Inch Battery Fan
amazonQuery: O2COOL Treva 10 inch battery powered fan with AC adapter
summary: A 10-inch, two-speed fan that runs on six D cells or the included AC adapter; the best choice for an emergency kit that may sit on a shelf for years.
verdict:
The O2COOL Treva 10-inch is the fan to keep in an emergency kit, because it runs on alkaline D cells that store for years and are sold almost everywhere.

**Why D cells still matter.** Lithium packs slowly lose charge on a shelf, and a fan you forgot to charge is useless the night a storm hits. The Treva takes six D cells, sold separately, which keep most of their charge for years in a cool closet. While the grid is up, run it from the included AC adapter and save the batteries. D cells are also the battery most likely to still be on store shelves the day before a hurricane.

**Simple, adequate cooling.** It has a 10-inch blade and two speeds, high and low. That is a clear step up from handheld fans and enough to keep one person comfortable at a bedside. Retailer listings quote roughly 20 to 50 hours on fresh cells depending on speed, but the figures conflict, so treat any single number as approximate. Six alkaline D cells hold more energy than a typical 10,000mAh [power bank](/best-portable-chargers-for-power-outages/).

**Battery care.** Store the cells outside the fan so they cannot leak into it, write the purchase date on the pack, and rotate them every few years. Keep a second set in the kit for a long outage.

Owners report it is light and easy to set up; the main complaint is that airflow drops as the cells drain. Compare it with tool-battery fans like the [Ryobi WhisperSeries](/gear/ryobi-one-plus-whisperseries-fan/) in the [best battery-powered fan](/best-battery-powered-fan/) roundup.

name: Geek Aire Rechargeable Outdoor Fan
amazonQuery: Geek Aire rechargeable outdoor high velocity fan
summary: A rechargeable high-velocity floor fan with a built-in battery; the simplest room-size cooling for households with no tool batteries and a summer outage plan.
verdict:
Geek Aire's rechargeable outdoor fan is the best pick here for a household that owns no tool batteries but wants real room-scale airflow when the power is out.

**A floor fan with a battery inside.** Geek Aire builds high-velocity floor fans in several sizes, commonly 10, 12 and 16 inches, with a built-in lithium battery and variable speed control. You charge it from the wall while the power is on, then run it cordless when it goes off. Many models also run straight from their AC adapter, and some add a USB port to top up a phone. Battery size and runtime vary a lot by model, so read the exact listing before you buy.

**Plan for the recharge.** A built-in battery cannot be swapped for a fresh one mid-outage. When it runs flat, you need power to refill it, which is where a [power station](/gear/jackery-explorer-1000-v2/) or a small solar panel fits in. Plug the fan's wattage and battery size into the [runtime calculator](/tools/power-station-runtime-calculator/) to see how many refills a station gives you. Run it on a middle speed overnight; high drains any battery several times faster than low.

**Where it fits.** It is heavier and louder than personal fans like the [Jisulife handheld](/gear/jisulife-handheld-fan/), but it moves enough air for a bedroom, patio or garage. If you already own Ryobi or DeWalt packs, a tool fan is cheaper.

Owners report strong airflow and solid build; the main complaints are weight and short runtime on high. It is part of our [best battery-powered fan](/best-battery-powered-fan/) roundup.

name: Jisulife Handheld Fan
summary: A pocket-size USB-C rechargeable fan that cools one face at close range; cheap enough to buy one per person for hot, powerless nights and summer outings.
verdict:
A Jisulife handheld fan is the cheapest way to make a hot, powerless night bearable, as long as you expect it to cool a face rather than a room.

**What it does well.** Jisulife is one of the best-selling handheld fan brands, and its Life-series fans charge over USB-C and fit in a pocket. Current models typically offer several speeds, often five. During an outage, one becomes a bedside fan pointed at your pillow; the rest of the year it rides along to ballgames, theme parks and hot commutes.

**Battery math is on your side.** A handheld with a 3,600mAh to 5,000mAh cell stores roughly 13 to 19 [watt-hours](/glossary/watt-hours/). That is small, but these fans sip power, so Life9 listings quote about 8.5 to 12 hours on low and only a few hours on the top speed. A 10,000mAh power bank can refill one about twice, and a [power station](/gear/anker-solix-c1000/) can keep a whole family's fans charged for days.

**Buy the right model.** Lineups and battery sizes change often, so favor listings that state capacity. For room-scale airflow, step up to a floor fan like the [Geek Aire](/gear/geek-aire-rechargeable-fan/) or a [20-inch box fan on a power station](/gear/lasko-3733-box-fan/).

Owners report it is handy and well made for the price; the main complaint is short runtime on high. It is the handheld pick in our [best battery-powered fan](/best-battery-powered-fan/) roundup, and pairs well with our [portable chargers](/best-portable-chargers-for-power-outages/) guide.

faqs.q: Is a handheld fan enough during a summer power outage?
faqs.a: For one person at close range, yes; for a room, no. A handheld fan moves air across your face and neck, which helps you sleep, but it will not lower the room temperature. Buy one per person and pair them with a larger fan, such as a box fan on a power station, for the room.

name: Lasko 3733 20-Inch Box Fan
summary: A plain 20-inch, three-speed box fan that draws about 80 watts on high; on a mid-size power station it moves more air per watt-hour than any battery fan.
verdict:
The Lasko 3733 is not a battery fan, and that is the point: paired with a power station, it is the most air you can buy for a summer outage.

**Big air, modest watts.** It is a 20-inch, three-speed box fan sold in nearly every hardware store. Retailers list it at about 80 to 83 watts on high, with Lasko's Save-Smart claim of under 2 cents an hour to run, and Home Depot lists it at about 1,800 CFM. That is several times the airflow of any battery fan on this page.

**Run it from a power station.** Divide the station's [watt-hours](/glossary/watt-hours/) by the fan's draw, then allow about 15% for inverter losses. A 1,000Wh station such as the [Jackery Explorer 1000 v2](/gear/jackery-explorer-1000-v2/) runs it about 10 to 11 hours at 80 watts, and longer on a lower speed. A 300Wh unit still gives about three hours on high. The [runtime calculator](/tools/power-station-runtime-calculator/) does this math for any station.

**Where it loses.** The inverter burns some energy just staying on, so on very small batteries a DC fan wins. It is also bulky to store at about 20.5 by 21.75 inches and roughly 7 pounds. At night, set it in a window to pull in cooler outside air.

Owners report it is cheap, simple and reliable; the main complaint is noise on high. See where it ranks in the [best battery-powered fan](/best-battery-powered-fan/) roundup.

name: Makita DCF102Z 18V LXT Fan
summary: Makita's 18V LXT fan with a 7-1/8 inch blade, three speeds and automatic oscillation, rated up to 8 hours on high with a 5Ah pack; best for Makita owners.
verdict:
The Makita DCF102Z is the best tool-battery fan for anyone on Makita 18V LXT, and it adds something most cordless fans skip: automatic oscillation.

**It sweeps the room.** The head oscillates automatically, about 45° to each side, so one fan can cool two people in a bed or a couch and a chair. Makita lists three speeds and a top air volume of 4.6 cubic meters per minute, about 160 CFM, from a 7-1/8 inch blade. That is personal-to-small-room airflow, similar to the [Ryobi WhisperSeries](/gear/ryobi-one-plus-whisperseries-fan/) but spread wider.

**Strong runtime.** Makita rates it for up to 8 hours of continuous use on high with an 18V LXT 5.0Ah battery, and retailers quote up to about 21 hours on low with a 6Ah pack. A 5Ah LXT pack holds about 90 [watt-hours](/glossary/watt-hours/), so one battery covers a full night. It weighs about 4.3 pounds with a battery, light enough to move between rooms.

**What to buy with it.** The DCF102Z is tool-only, and the AC adapter that lets it run from the wall is sold separately. If you already own two or more LXT packs and a charger, it is an easy add-on; recharge packs from a [power station](/gear/anker-solix-c1000/) in longer outages. If you own no Makita batteries, a fan with a built-in battery is a simpler buy.

Owners report quiet running and handy oscillation; the main complaint is that the AC adapter costs extra. Compare battery fans in the [best battery-powered fan](/best-battery-powered-fan/) roundup.

name: Ryobi ONE+ 18V Bucket Top Misting Fan (PCL851B)
amazonQuery: Ryobi PCL851B ONE+ 18V bucket top misting fan
summary: A 7-1/2 inch ONE+ 18V fan that sits on a 5-gallon bucket and mists up to 14 feet; the outage pick for patios, porches and yard work in dry heat.
verdict:
The Ryobi PCL851B is the cooling tool for hot outage days outdoors: a fan that sits on top of a standard 5-gallon bucket and turns its water into a cooling mist.

**How it works.** Fill a bucket with water, set the fan on top, and it feeds a misting ring around the 7-1/2 inch blade. Ryobi rates it for up to 14 feet of misting coverage and 840 feet per minute of air velocity on high. The mist rate is listed at about 1.1 gallons per hour on low, so a full bucket lasts around four and a half hours on that setting. Evaporative cooling works best in dry heat; in very humid weather, the mist adds dampness more than relief.

**Battery and runtime.** It runs on any Ryobi ONE+ 18V battery, and Ryobi quotes more than 5 hours of continuous runtime. The bare tool is the PCL851B; the PCL851K kit adds a compact battery and charger. A 4Ah ONE+ pack holds about 72 [watt-hours](/glossary/watt-hours/), and larger packs stretch runtime further. Recharge packs from a [power station](/gear/jackery-explorer-1000-v2/) or a [generator](/best-gas-generator/) during long outages.

**Where not to use it.** Mist and indoor electronics or wood floors do not mix, so this is a porch, patio, garage or jobsite fan. For indoor sleeping, the [Ryobi WhisperSeries](/gear/ryobi-one-plus-whisperseries-fan/) on the same batteries is the better choice.

Owners report it is a refreshing way to work outside in the heat; the main complaint is that the bucket and water make it awkward to move. Browse more options in the [best battery-powered fan](/best-battery-powered-fan/) roundup.

faqs.q: How long does the Ryobi bucket top misting fan run?
faqs.a: Ryobi quotes more than 5 hours of continuous runtime, and runtime grows with larger ONE+ batteries. Water is the other limit: Ryobi lists a mist rate of about 1.1 gallons per hour on low, so a full 5-gallon bucket lasts roughly four and a half hours on that setting.

faqs.q: Can I use the Ryobi misting fan indoors?
faqs.a: It is designed for outdoor and open-air spaces like patios, garages and jobsites. Indoors, the mist can wet floors, furniture and electronics, and in a closed room it raises humidity quickly, which makes you feel warmer. For indoor cooling, use a dry fan such as the Ryobi WhisperSeries on the same ONE+ batteries.

name: Milwaukee M18 PACKOUT Fan (0818-20)
summary: Milwaukee's brushless M18 PACKOUT fan is rated at 850 CFM, runs on M18 packs or AC power, and locks onto PACKOUT storage; the high-airflow pick for M18 owners.
verdict:
The Milwaukee 0818-20 is the most powerful battery fan here, and for M18 owners it is the fan that can actually cool a living room.

**Room-scale airflow.** Milwaukee rates it at 850 CFM and up to 20.5 MPH air speed from a brushless motor, with variable speed control. That beats the [DeWalt DCE512B](/gear/dewalt-20v-max-jobsite-fan/) at 650 CFM and roughly doubles the [Milwaukee M12 fan](/gear/milwaukee-m12-compact-jobsite-fan/). It also runs on AC power through a standard extension cord with no battery installed, so it doubles as an everyday shop or bedroom fan.

**Runtime on high is short.** Milwaukee quotes over 3 hours on high and 6.5 hours at 75% speed with an XC5.0 battery. An M18 5Ah pack holds about 90 [watt-hours](/glossary/watt-hours/), which implies a draw of up to about 30 watts on high. For an overnight outage, run it slower or use a 12Ah pack. In a long outage, a [power station](/gear/anker-solix-c1000/) can recharge packs or run the fan directly through its AC cord.

**Built for the PACKOUT system.** It weighs about 6.4 pounds and locks onto Milwaukee PACKOUT boxes, which keeps it stable on a stack in a garage or truck. If you do not own PACKOUT or M18, you pay for features you will not use.

Owners report it moves serious air for its size; the main complaints are price and fast battery drain on high. Compare it in the [best battery-powered fan](/best-battery-powered-fan/) roundup.

faqs.q: How long does the Milwaukee M18 PACKOUT fan run?
faqs.a: Milwaukee rates the 0818-20 for over 3 hours on high and 6.5 hours at 75% speed with an M18 XC5.0 battery. Larger packs scale that up; a 12Ah pack holds well over twice the energy. It also runs on AC power through an extension cord, with no battery needed, when the grid or a generator is available.

faqs.q: Is the Milwaukee PACKOUT fan better than the DeWalt DCE512B?
faqs.a: It moves more air, 850 CFM versus DeWalt's 650 CFM rating, and it can run on AC power, which the cordless-only DCE512B cannot. The DeWalt runs a bit longer on high, up to 4.5 hours on a 5Ah pack versus just over 3 hours for the Milwaukee on an XC5.0. Buy the one that matches the batteries you own.
